title: Pan-Seared Seabass with Lemon Butter Sauce
description: Pan-Seared Seabass with Lemon Butter Sauce is a refined continental seafood dish featuring crispy skin, moist flaky flesh, and a silky beurre blanc-style lemon butter sauce. Finished with seasonal vegetables and elegant garnishes, it is a classic fine-dining restaurant favorite.

ingredients.title: For the Lemon Butter Sauce (Beurre Blanc style)
items: 2 tbsp white wine vinegar (or champagne vinegar)
120 g unsalted cold butter (cut into small cubes)

ingredients.title: For Garnish / Presentation
items: Lemon wedges or thin lemon slices (charred for sophistication)
Seasonal vegetables (blanched asparagus, baby carrots, or French beans)
Micro herbs or edible flowers (optional for fine dining plating)

instruction.title: 1. Prepare the Seabass
steps: Pat the seabass fillets dry with paper towels to ensure crispy skin.
Season both sides lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet (preferably stainless steel or cast iron) over medium-high heat.
Add olive oil and let it shimmer. Place the seabass skin-side down.
Press gently with a spatula to prevent curling. Cook 3–4 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip, add 1 tbsp butter, and baste for 1–2 minutes until flesh is opaque and moist.
Remove from pan and rest briefly on a warm plate.

instruction.title: 2. Make the Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: In a saucepan, combine shallots, white wine, and vinegar. Reduce over medium heat until only 2–3 tbsp of liquid remain.
Stir in heavy cream (optional) to stabilize the emulsion.
Lower heat to very gentle and whisk in butter cubes, one at a time, until the sauce is smooth and glossy. Do not let it boil.
Add lemon juice and zest, season with salt and white pepper. Strain through a fine sieve for a silky texture.

instruction.title: 3. Plate & Serve (Restaurant Style)
steps: Spoon a pool of lemon butter sauce onto a warm plate.
Place the seabass fillet skin-side up for crispness.
Arrange seasonal vegetables neatly to the side (blanched and glazed lightly in butter).
Garnish with dill sprigs, charred lemon wedge, and microgreens for an elegant finish.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Pair with a crisp dry white wine (e.g., Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay).

chefTips: Use super fresh seabass – skin should be crisp, flesh moist and tender.
Rest the fish briefly before plating to retain juiciness.
Sauce should be velvety, glossy, and smooth – strain for finesse.
Serve on warm plates to maintain texture and temperature.
